s: Today we talk about colors and feelings.
Colors can change how we feel.
A bright room makes me happy.
A dark room makes me sleepy.
And some days are bright, and some days are awful.
The weather was awful, and my bus was late, and my coffee was cold.
A bad day can feel awful.
But a bad day is not a bad life.
A bad morning can become a good evening.
I like bright colors when I feel bad.
I wear a bright yellow shirt, and I feel better.
A bright shirt is like sunshine.
A bright kitchen makes breakfast happy.
A bright smile makes friends happy.

Lena, when was the last time you felt confused?
Last week I was confused in a new city.
I was confused by the map.
I was confused by the signs.
Everything was confused in my head.
I was confused when I learned to cook.
I was confused by the recipe, and the kitchen was a mess.
And what about the word depressed?
After my team lost the big game, I felt depressed for a day.
When my friend moved to another city, I felt depressed too.
But a bad week does not mean you are depressed.
Depressed is a deep, heavy feeling.
If someone feels depressed for a long time, they should talk to a friend or a doctor.
Let me tell you about an awful movie I saw last week.
The story was bad, the actors were bad, and the ending was awful.
An awful movie is the worst.
But a bad movie can be fun with good friends.
Now, bright is my favorite word today.
Let us paint the kitchen bright yellow.
A bright kitchen is a great idea.
Bright colors make small rooms look big and happy.
And what about a bright future?
When we learn English every day, our future is bright.
A bright future for everyone who practices.
I remember an awful winter day.
The sky was gray, the streets were cold, and I felt so bad.
Then my friend called me, and we laughed, and the awful day became a bright evening.
So the words today are awful, bad, bright, confused, and depressed.
Bad is the opposite of good.
Bright is full of light and strong color.
Confused is when you cannot understand something.

Last year I was confused at the airport.
I was confused by the signs in a new language.
A kind man helped me, and I was not confused anymore.
And remember, an awful day can turn into a bright day.
A bad morning is not forever.
Try to use the words this week.
Tell a friend about a bright morning, or a bad movie, or an awful Monday.
And if you ever feel confused, just ask.
Asking questions is how we learn.
